verdicts.claim: By default SQLite runs an automatic checkpoint when a COMMIT leaves the WAL at 1000 pages or more, and when the last database connection closes
verdicts.evidence: wal.html 3.1: 'automatically checkpoint whenever a COMMIT occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more in size, or when the last database connection on a database file closes'; threshold changeable via wal_autocheckpoint / sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint()

verdicts.claim: All checkpoints from sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and the automatic mechanism are PASSIVE. FULL, RESTART and TRUNCATE are reachable only through v2/PRAGMA
verdicts.evidence: wal.html 3.2: 'All checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE. FULL and RESTART ... can only be initiated by a call to sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2()'; v2 page: 'PRAGMA wal_checkpoint command can be used to invoke this interface'

verdicts.claim: PASSIVE checkpoints as many frames as possible without waiting and never invokes the busy handler. FULL waits for no active writer...
verdicts.evidence: v2 page defines PASSIVE ('busy-handler callback is never invoked'), FULL, RESTART ('next writer will restart the log file'), TRUNCATE ('truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return')

verdicts.claim: If the busy handler returns 0 while a FULL, RESTART or TRUNCATE checkpoint waits for the writer lock or readers, the checkpoint continues as PASSIVE
verdicts.evidence: v2 page: 'proceeds from that point in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE ... SQLITE_BUSY is returned'; concurrent checkpoint lock -> SQLITE_BUSY, 'busy-handler ... will not be invoked in this case'

verdicts.claim: A completed checkpoint normally does not shrink the -wal file. SQLite rewinds and overwrites it from the start because overwriting is faster
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless the journal_size_limit pragma is set)... normally faster to overwrite an existing file'; Litestream: file 'retains its high-water size on disk'

verdicts.claim: The WAL is reset only when the checkpoint has transferred and synced the entire WAL and no reader uses it; the writer checks this on each write
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'Whenever a write operation occurs, the writer checks ... if the entire WAL has been transferred into the database and synced and if no readers are making use of the WAL, then the writer will rewind'; forum #142: 'If there is a write after checkpoint started, it can't be finished'

verdicts.claim: Checkpoints sync: the WAL is synced before pages move to the database... With synchronous=NORMAL the checkpoint is the only operation issuing an I/O barrier
verdicts.evidence: wal.html 2.3: 'WAL must be synced ... prior to moving content ... database file must be synced prior to resetting the WAL'; 'with PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, the checkpoint is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier ... transactions are no longer durable'

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint returns one row of three integers: busy, WAL frames, frames checkpointed. After a successful TRUNCATE both counts are 0; Syncthing flagged April 2025
verdicts.evidence: forum #158 (Apr 3 2025, bt90): 'We don't check the return values of PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(RESTART)' quoting the three-column row; v2 page: after TRUNCATE 'both *pnLog and *pnCkpt will be set to zero'

verdicts.claim: If a database always has at least one active reader, no checkpoint completes and the WAL grows without bound. Docs suggest reader gaps or RESTART/TRUNCATE
verdicts.evidence: wal.html checkpoint starvation: 'there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound'; recommends reader gaps and RESTART/TRUNCATE with blocking downside

verdicts.claim: The wal.html page notes a WAL-reset bug in 3.7.0 through 3.51.2, fixed in 3.51.3
verdicts.evidence: wal.html section 11: '3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09). It is fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) and later' (claim is uncited in draft but names wal.html)
